question: Does a published, peer-reviewed quantum reservoir design (Domingo, Grande, Carlo, Borondo, Borondo, 'Optimal quantum reservoir computing for market forecasting: an application to fight food price crises', Eng. Appl. Artif. Intell. 182, 2026, doi:10.1016/j.engappai.2026.115854; arXiv:2401.03347) beat a matched classical reservoir and the HAR benchmark on copper volatility at any sampling frequency from 5 minutes to daily?
motivation: All earlier copper results use a quantum reservoir designed inside this project (angle encoding, no memory between bins). A reviewer can say it was a weak quantum model. The Domingo design is external, published as optimal by its authors, and has memory (the state is carried from one bar to the next).
not_a_reproduction: This is the authors' DESIGN applied to a different task. They forecast a weekly agricultural price level (356 training weeks, 62 test weeks, MAE and direction accuracy). Here the target is volatility and the data are copper. No statement about their zucchini result follows from this run. Source read: arXiv preprint in full; published 2026 version at abstract level only (its comparison with classical models is not in the preprint).
extends: long_prereg_hf.json, long_prereg_hf2.json (intraday grids H, M, F; fixed mode) and long_prereg_dbdaily.json (daily Databento range target). Same data files, rows, targets, benchmarks, splits, purge, readouts, statistics and verdict words. No earlier result is recomputed or changed; earlier models are read from their stored prediction files.

models.DOM: dom_lib.features(..., 'G3'). 7 qubits; qubit 0 carries the input u in [0,1] as sqrt(1-u)|0> + sqrt(u)|1>; each step the other 6 qubits keep the state (partial trace over qubit 0), then a fixed random circuit of 150 gates from G3 = {CNOT, H, T}. Features: <X_i> and <Z_i> of the 7 qubits after gate 75 and after gate 150 (Nv = 2), 28 features. Exact density-matrix result (two Kraus operators on the 6-qubit memory; equal to the direct 7-qubit simulation to 1e-10, dom_lib.selftest). Values N = 7, Nv = 2, about 150 gates and family G3 are the paper's stated optimum.
models.DOMG1: Same gate layout and seeds with family G1 = {CNOT, H, X} (the paper's least complex family). Tests the paper's claim that higher circuit complexity gives better forecasts.
models.ESN28u: dom_lib.esn1: leaky echo state network, 28 units, the same single input (standardised), spectral radius 0.9, leak 0.5, input scale 0.5 (the fixed values of long_prereg_hf.json). Matched classical reservoir: same input, same feature count, also has memory.
models.input: ONE series: ln realised variance of the current bin (intraday) or ln daily range variance (daily). Missing values hold the last value. DOM/DOMG1: linear min-max scaling to [0,1] with the minimum and maximum of TRAINING rows only (as the paper), clipped. ESN28u: standardised with training mean and sd. Reservoirs run recurrently along the block's bins (intraday: from the first usable row of year Y-4; daily: from the first day).
models.readout_intraday: As hf2_run.py: ridge on the 28 features (lambda from {1e-2,1e-1,1,10,100,1000} on validation) fitted to the residual of the HAR + hour-of-day benchmark and added back; forecasts averaged over 10 seeds (0-9).
models.readout_daily: As db_run.py: HAR features plus the 28 reservoir features, linear model with QLIKE loss anchored on lvR5, ridge from (1e-3,1e-2,1e-1,1,10) on validation, 10 seeds averaged, validation-calibrated scale.
models.no_tuning: No hyperparameter of DOM, DOMG1 or ESN28u is tuned (only the ridge strength, on validation). Stored comparison models are their FIXED configurations on H, M, F (like for like) and their tuned configurations on D (the only stored daily version).
models.interpretations_of_the_paper: The preprint does not give the gate-sampling rule or how intermediate times are defined for a gate circuit. Chosen here before any result: each gate type uniform over the three family members, qubits uniform (CNOT control and target distinct); the intermediate readout is after half the gates.

blocks.intraday: Grids H (60 min), M (15 min), F (5 min) from data/hf/*.npz (licensed Databento; not redistributed). Test year Y in 2013..2025 (13 blocks per grid), validation Y-1, training Y-4..Y-2, 24 h purge. Regimes: tertiles of mean ln RV (4 calm, 5 intermediate, 4 turbulent), as before.
blocks.daily: Grid D: data/daily_databento/HG_db_1d_range.csv, target ln of 5-day forward mean range variance, ten one-year blocks 2015-2024, expanding window, validation 2 years before, purge 5 rows. Regimes 3/4/3 by annualised volatility.
blocks.heldout: After the rolling report is written: intraday 2026 (to 2026-10-16) on H, M, F; daily 2025 and 2026 (to 2026-10-06 after the target horizon). For the daily held-out years the earlier daily models are produced by dom_dbheldout.py (db_run.py with only the output locations changed).

statistics: As before. Intraday: per-row squared error of ln RV; daily: QLIKE with validation-calibrated scale. Ratio of mean losses with a Diebold-Mariano HAC interval (lags H 24, M 96, F 288, D 10); +/-3% equivalence band; verdict words on the interval; Holm within family and stratum. Families: A primary = DOM vs ESN28u, DOM vs DOMG1, DOM vs benchmark (HAR + hour-of-day, or HARq on D); B stored models = DOM vs earlier quantum reservoir (QRC / QRC_angle), RandFeat, ESN, TrigFeat; C descriptive = ESN28u vs benchmark, DOMG1 vs benchmark; H (daily held-out only) = earlier quantum reservoir QRC_angle vs ESN, QRC_noent, RandFeat, TrigFeat, HARq on 2025-26. Strata: all, calm, intermediate, turbulent (rolling); all (held-out).

decision_rules.quantum_edge: On a grid, an edge of the Domingo design is claimed only if DOM beats ESN28u AND the benchmark pooled over all blocks (whole 95% interval below 1 and Holm p < 0.05 for each) AND DOM's ratio is below 1 against both in the turbulent stratum. Evaluated per grid; dom_report.py prints it.
decision_rules.complexity_claim: Supported on a grid if DOM vs DOMG1 has its whole interval below 1 with Holm p < 0.05. Otherwise not supported on copper volatility.
decision_rules.frequency_effect: Descriptive only: whether DOM vs ESN28u moves across F, M, H, D. No trend test.
decision_rules.heldout: The held-out step CONFIRMS a no-edge conclusion if the pooled rule is not met on any grid in the held-out data. A held-out edge without a rolling edge is reported as an isolated result. Family H is the first scoring of the earlier quantum reservoir on daily Databento data after 2024.
decision_rules.family_B: Context only. The stored models read 8 inputs (H, M, F) or 6 inputs (D) and have 36 or 21 features; DOM reads one input and has 28. A difference there is not a quantum-versus-classical result.

student_prediction.reading: NOT stated. The student was asked for a prediction and answered 'approved, go ahead and run it'. Left null and not filled in on the student's behalf.

claude_prediction_recorded_for_transpare.text: No edge on any grid. DOM vs ESN28u within about 1% (equivalent) or ESN28u slightly better; DOM vs DOMG1 equivalent, so the complexity claim is not supported; all three single-input reservoirs add less than 2% to the benchmark and do worse than the stored multi-input models. Held-out data show the same pattern; family H gives ties or inconclusive results for the earlier quantum reservoir.

checks_done_before_registration: Nothing scored. (1) dom_lib.selftest on random numbers: Kraus propagation equals the direct 7-qubit simulation; circuits unitary; G3 and G1 features differ. (2) dom_run.py H 2015 with DRY=1: feature shapes and finiteness on 3000 bins, no forecast made. (3) Row counts: H 2015 test rows 5303, equal to the stored file; daily block sizes for 2015, 2024, 2025, 2026 printed. (4) dom_report.py comparison and Holm functions on synthetic numbers. dom_report.py stops if rows, targets or benchmark forecasts differ from the stored run.
known_limits: Not blind: every earlier copper result (ties, no edge), including the 2026 intraday block for the earlier models, was seen before this design. The 2026 intraday block is therefore not a fresh test of the earlier models; DOM, DOMG1 and ESN28u have not been scored on it. Daily 2025-26 on the Databento target has not been scored for any reservoir model before this run.
The authors' design, not their experiment: different target, asset, sample size and readout (residual add-on to a benchmark). Two details of the circuit are my interpretation (see models).
Min-max scaling over tens of thousands of training rows puts most inputs in a narrow part of [0,1]; this follows the paper but may limit the reservoir's response. It is not tuned here.
One input only, as in the paper's first scenario. The paper's second scenario (extra regressor variables appended to the features) is not run.
Exact simulation: no shots, no device noise. The paper's noise analysis is not repeated.
Copper only; blocks overlap in training data; few turbulent blocks; HAC intervals are narrow at intraday sample sizes, so small differences are not economically meaningful.
AI-written code, not independently re-derived by the student. Licensed data are not committed.
cost_estimate: Estimate, not measurement: about 0.5 ms per reservoir step; about 20 CPU-hours in total, mostly the 5-minute grid; no hardware jobs; no new data.
stop_rule: One run of the registered jobs (39 intraday and 10 daily rolling blocks, then 7 held-out jobs), report and stop. No new models, grids, seeds, gate counts or scalings after results. A crashed job is re-run unchanged.
